name: Automotive Electrical Technology
short_description: This qualification reflects the role of individuals who perform a broad range of tasks on a variety of light vehicles in the automotive retail, service and repair industry.
hero_description: Are you working 20+ hours per week performing automotive electrical services in vehicles? With Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), you can use your existing skills and work experience to gain this qualification without classroom study.
overview: If your work involves performing a range of services, diagnosing and repairing electrical systems and components in vehicles in the automotive electrical service and repair industry, then, certifying your skills with an AUR30320 – Certificate III in Automotive Electrical Technology qualification can significantly enhance your career prospects. This qualification can open doors to roles such as Automotive Electrical Technician. These positions not only come with greater responsibilities but also offer higher pay, as many employers prefer and reward employees with recognized qualifications. By formalizing your experience through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), you position yourself for long-term success and advancement in this expanding sector.

faq.question: Who can apply for RPL?
answer: Seasoned Professionals: Individuals with extensive experience in their field but lacking a current formal qualification.
Experienced Workers: Workers who began their careers before formal qualifications became a requirement.
Qualification Upgraders: Professionals seeking to upgrade their qualifications by having their practical experience recognized.
Career Progressors (CPD): Employees aiming to advance in their careers by formally validating their skills.
Advanced Learners: Individuals looking to pursue further education who can obtain course credits by demonstrating existing expertise in the qualification units.

faq.question: Comprehensive Evidence for RPL in Certificate III in Automotive Electrical Technology?
answer: Below is the list of documents we need from you to review and submit to the RTO for your RPL assessment application:

100 Points of ID: Accepted documents include: driver’s license, passport, Medicare card, proof of age card, key pass, and utility bills (For more information, refer to the guidelines on 100 Points of ID)
Updated Resume: With your current skills, experiences, and employment history (more info)
USI Number: If you don’t have one, you can create one at www.usi.gov.au
Employment Contracts or Job Offer Letters
Reference letter from your employer or senior management, detailing your job description (must be on company letterhead)
Pay slips or invoices (optional) with your name.
Academic documents with transcripts (Ex: first aid, diploma, bachelor, certificate ii, iii, iv, year 12 certificate etc.)
Working with Children Check (if applicable)

Additional Supporting Evidence: This could include: Excel files, plans, other work samples, or any documentation aligned with the unit outline to demonstrate your competency in the applied qualification.

Important Notes: The RTO may contact you for further evidence. An RTO assessor might conduct a competency interview. Gap training may be required to address any areas of improvement and ensure a positive assessment outcome.
